title: The Propagation–Failure Quotient (PFQ)
description:
Subtitle: A Diagnostic Platform for Virality, Containment, and Systemic Failure
Project Description (OSF)
The Propagation–Failure Quotient (PFQ) is a diagnostic platform that classifies spreading phenomena after the fact, using observable effects rather than intent, narrative, or ideology.
PFQ distinguishes two orthogonal dimensions: how something propagates (lightning vs plasma) and where systems fail (plague vs cancer). Together, these dimensions form a diamond geometry that enables post-hoc classification of viral events, institutional breakdowns, and adoption dynamics without requiring predictive claims or moral interpretation.
The platform does not absorb or replace other projects. It remains independent and usable across domains—science, media, institutions, technology, and culture—providing a minimal quotient output that identifies the propagation regime and failure origin from empirical patterns alone.
PFQ is designed to reduce category error, prevent premature theorizing, and support responsible diagnosis when “something is burning,” without assuming why it started or who is responsible.
